long_biography.plain_text:
Goldstein entered the ski trade in the late 1970s and established Nevica as a distributor before turning it into a skiwear label. Bright technical clothing became the brand's signature, while licensing the Killy name widened its premium reach. He remained chairman as Nevica prepared a successor label after the Killy agreement ended.

Property became a second operating career. Goldstein moved from financing developments to directing them through EandO, concentrating on luxury homes in London and other international markets. In 2010, he sold Nevica's worldwide brand rights to Sports Direct. His continuing directorships in Nevica and EandO show how apparel and property have remained connected in his corporate portfolio.

uncertainties.detail: The direct yacht-service and Barche profiles bridge La Cima III to the Nevica founder and EandO developer, while Companies House resolves the exact name as Paul Joseph Goldstein, born July 1955. The British wildlife photographer and safari operator, American tennis player, Stanford professor, US lawyer, 1968-born UK photography-company director and other same-name professionals were excluded.

Companies House independently repeats July 1955 across the matching Nevica and EandO officer identities, supporting the month and year. No strong reviewed source provides the exact day or place of birth, so those fields remain blank.

Drapers reports that Goldstein sold Nevica's worldwide brand rights to Sports Direct in 2010, while Companies House still lists him as the active director of the original Nevica Limited company. The dossier distinguishes the transferred consumer brand rights from the continuing legal entity and does not infer current brand control.

Current registry records support active EandO property development and continuing Nevica and investment directorships, but private accounts do not reveal the relative value of each interest. Real Estate is selected because EandO is his clearest current operating business and the direct profile documents a deliberate career transition into development.

Focused searches found more than one hundred LinkedIn profiles and many Instagram, Facebook and X namesakes, none with sufficient Nevica, EandO and July 1955 identity markers. No personal website or dedicated Wikipedia page was verified, and the EandO domain was not sufficiently attributable as a current official destination.

Exact-name and profile-path searches found no dedicated Forbes person profile for the Nevica founder. Forbes contributor articles and image credits involving the same-name wildlife photographer were excluded.

Secondary nationality, optional title and suffix, secondary residence, exact birth day and birthplace remain unresolved rather than inferred. Death fields remain inapplicable because current verified directorships are consistent with the saved Alive status.

La Cima III was used only to bridge the saved owner to the Nevica and EandO entrepreneur. No vessel name, specification, builder, movements or ownership history appears in either biography or supports any wealth or tag conclusion.
